hypothesis_1.hypothesis: H1: Longer resolution times significantly reduce member satisfaction
hypothesis_1.business_conclusion: Statistically significant negative correlation (rho = -0.4628, p = 0.00e+00). Every 10-minute increase in resolution duration is associated with a measurable degradation in member satisfaction ratings. Operational efforts to reduce handle times directly improve CSAT.

hypothesis_2.hypothesis: H2: Members with multiple contacts have a higher escalation probability
hypothesis_2.test_type: Welch's Two-Sample t-test (unequal variances) & Mann-Whitney U
hypothesis_2.business_conclusion: Statistically significant difference confirmed (t = 32.0523, p = 2.48e-182, Cohen's d = 1.167). Escalated interactions averaged 2.88 contacts vs. 1.60 contacts for non-escalated cases. Failing to resolve inquiries on the primary contact exponentially increases escalation risk.

hypothesis_3.hypothesis: H3: Digital channels have lower escalation rates than voice calls
hypothesis_3.test_type: Pearson Chi-Square Test of Independence & Odds Ratio
hypothesis_3.business_conclusion: Statistically significant difference confirmed (Chi2 = 338.0008, p = 1.74e-75, df = 1). Digital channels exhibited an escalation rate of 10.69% versus 25.22% for Voice calls. Voice interactions have 2.82x higher odds of escalation (95% CI: [2.52, 3.16]). Care navigation strategies should route initial triage to asynchronous and interactive digital channels.
